_about: Inputs to tools/palette/generate.mjs. Pinned values are agreed colors, copied once (2026-10-07) from brand-v2-working: gray from src/pages/rounds/_working.ts GRAY (the surfaces round's display-adjusted values), hues from src/pages/rounds/color/_palettes.json palette 'ink' (written by brand-v2-lab generate.py). Edit here, then regenerate; never edit tokens/ generated files by hand.

saturation._note: Per-mode chroma factor on every hue step and fitted gradient stop (color round, 2026-09-25). Gray takes no offset. Dark was 0.95 until 2026-10-09; set to 1 (no desaturation) to try a less muted dark mode (Bennett, 2026-10-08), exploring.

new._rule: OKLCH lerp from gray 200 to gray 600 at t

midtone_boost._rule: Applied after pinning and lerp, to every gray step: chroma += amount × exp(−(L − center)² / (2 · width²)), L on 0–100, each step's own L and H kept; chroma pulled back to fit sRGB if needed. Set amount 0 to turn it off.
midtone_boost._note: Default from 2026-10-12 (Bennett and Kyle): the Color page's suggested boost with the center moved from 58 to 54. Exploring; judge it in context.

red._note: Exploring (Kyle, 2026-10-12): red pulled slightly toward rose to read as OpenMined's red rather than a generic one. Re-keyed to oklch(0.55 0.17 20.6) as the light-mode key: every pinned step's OKLCH hue rotated -3.7° and its chroma scaled × 1.033 (base key chroma 0.150 → 0.155, × 1.1 in light), lightness kept, so the shared lightness ladder holds. A first try at hue 16.8 read too pink and was dropped the same day. The previous red is kept below as backup_2026_10_12: to restore it, move it back to pinned.

100.was: red 100: #ffefee, hue 21.8 → 18.1, chroma × 1.033, lightness kept, gamut-mapped

200.was: red 200: #ffd1cd, hue 24.0 → 20.3, chroma × 1.033, lightness kept, gamut-mapped

backup_2026_10_12._note: The agreed Ink red (key hue 24.3) before the rose trial. Not read by the generator.

50._rule: a lighter wash: L 98.4, chroma 0.45 x step 100, hue of 100

400._rule: OKLCH midpoint of 300 and the key (500)

900._rule: dark-mode fill: L 22, chroma 0.8 x step 800, hue of 800

950._rule: L 16.5, chroma 0.62 x step 800, hue of 800

gradient._note: Family stops are the hue's key; fitted stops (no family) carry their own base value and take the saturation offset. Extra stops are tokens for graphics but stay out of the spectrum. Lists are each graphic's own stops, in the order that graphic uses them; generated as gradient tokens (gradient.flow, gradient.map).

extra.name: magenta
extra._from: Graphics-only stop, not in the spectrum. Sampled from the live site's CTA raster, left side (openmined.org/images/cta-gradient-bg.png, 2026-10-09: #b83e7c, OKLCH H353 C.168 L55). v1's rose red and orchid violet blended into it; v2's red (H24) and violet (H300) leave an 84° gap. The palette red moved slightly toward it on 2026-10-12 (key hue 24.3 → 20.6, exploring; design/decisions/2026-10-12-red-toward-rose.md).

flow._for: The colorflow (<om-stream>): six stops in the order the site's home hero uses.

interactive._for: Color that moves behind a white label (button hover, motion round option F): the wheel in hue keys only, green → teal → blue → violet → red → amber → green, so the label never drops below the green key's contrast (about 3.8:1). The spectrum's fitted stops (gold, orange, lime, yellow) stay for graphics; white on them is 1.3–2.5:1 (2026-10-13).

map._for: The gradient map (<om-mesh>): one color per point, in the embed's point order (top, top left, left, bottom-left corner, bottom left, bottom middle, bottom right, right). Matches the live raster: magenta on the left, no blue (Bennett, 2026-10-08: 'red on the left is too red, blue area too heavy'). A list entry is a gradient stop name, or a hue step such as violet.400.

two_tone._note: One two-tone gradient per palette hue (gradient.two-tone-<hue>), for icons and any other use that names a primary hue: the hue's key, its darker step, the companion, its lighter step, its key. The companion is chosen per hue, not the next hue around the wheel (Kyle and Bennett, 2026-10-12: gold to green read as a big color change, not a hue shift; gold takes red). Generated in both modes.
two_tone._companions: red, amber, green and blue as reviewed on the icons (motion round E, gold changed to red; blue changed to teal, 2026-10-14); teal and violet are first guesses, not yet seen in use. 2026-10-26 (Kyle): blue takes violet, green takes gradient lime, amber takes gradient gold, teal takes green.
two_tone._companion_values: A companion is a hue (it takes steps.<mode>.companion) or a gradient stop written gradient.<stop> (gold, orange, lime, yellow, magenta …), which has one value per mode and no steps (Kyle, 2026-10-26: diagrams are graphics, so the graphics colors are fair companions).
two_tone._steps: Which step of the hue (and of its companion) each stop takes, per mode. Light keeps the key and 500, takes 300 for the lighter stop and 400 for the companion (Kyle, 2026-10-14: 400 for both still read subtle in light; one step lighter throughout read washed out).

highlight._note: One highlight per palette hue (gradient.highlight-<hue>): the brighter, more energetic part of a moving line in that hue, such as the pulse along a diagram line or a ring. It reads as the same line lit up, not a second color, so each is chosen to be lighter than its hue in both modes, toward yellow on the wheel. Separate from the two-tone companions, which pass a second color through an icon or a card (Kyle, 2026-10-27: violet's red and blue's violet read as other colors on the diagrams).
highlight._colors: 2026-10-27 (Kyle): red, amber, green and teal as their two-tone companions, which already read as highlights on the diagrams; blue takes teal, violet takes blue; then violet takes its own 300 (blue's dark key barely lifted the line), then the gradient's magenta (300 didn't read right; magenta approved on the diagrams). A value is a hue (it takes steps.<mode>), a hue at its own step (violet.300, both modes) or a gradient stop, gradient.<stop>.
highlight._steps: The step a hue highlight takes, per mode: the same as the two-tone companion step.

shadows._about: The surfaces round's settled ladder (brand-v2-lab DECISIONS 2026-09-17/18): one rung per level, base casts nothing; ink is a gray step per mode, never a typed color. Geometry in px: [offsetX, offsetY, blur, spread].
